title: Multiple Linear Regression I
description: Recall deck covering least squares, model assumptions, goodness of fit, inference, and special explanatory variables from Chapter 3. This is part one of a two-part series.

cards.front: What is the general multiple linear regression fitted plane?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What quantity does the method of least squares minimize in multiple regression?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: In matrix notation, what are the dimensions of \(\mathbf{y}\) and \(\mathbf{X}\)?
cards.back: \(\mathbf{y}\) is an \(n\times1\) response vector, and \(\mathbf{X}\) is an \(n\times(k+1)\) explanatory-variable matrix.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What role does \(x_{i0}\) usually play in the design matrix?
cards.back: It is associated with the intercept and is usually identically equal to \(1\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What are the normal equations for least squares regression?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Under what condition does the unique least squares solution \(\mathbf{b}=(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}\) exist?
cards.back: When the explanatory variables are not linear combinations of one another, so \(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}\) is invertible.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: In the term life regression of LNFACE on EDUCATION, NUMHH, and LNINCOME, what fitted plane was obtained?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: How is \(\beta_j\) interpreted for a continuous explanatory variable?
cards.back: It is the expected change in \(y\) per unit change in \(x_j\), holding all other explanatory variables fixed.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What does the intercept \(\beta_0\) represent in the usual model with \(x_0=1\)?
cards.back: The expected value of \(y\) when all explanatory variables equal zero; it sets the height of the fitted regression plane.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: In a log-response model, what does a small change in \(\ln y\) approximate?
cards.back: A small proportional change in \(y\), since \(\partial\ln y/\partial x=(\partial y/\partial x)/y\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the economic interpretation of \(\partial\ln y/\partial\ln x\)?
cards.back: It is an elasticity: the ratio of the percentage change in \(y\) to the percentage change in \(x\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: ______ is the coefficient interpretation for a binary variable: the expected increase in \(y\) when moving from the base level \(0\) to the alternative level \(1\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Under assumptions F1--F5, what is the distribution of \(\mathbf{b}\)?
cards.back: The least squares estimator \(\mathbf{b}\) is normally distributed.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What does the Gauss-Markov theorem say about least squares estimators?
cards.back: Among estimators that are linear functions of the responses, least squares is the minimum-variance unbiased estimator of \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is a residual?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the mean square error estimator \(s^2\) of \(\sigma^2\)?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the residual standard deviation?
cards.back: \(s=\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{n-(k+1)}\sum_{i=1}^ne_i^2}\); it is also called the standard error of the estimate.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Why does the MSE denominator use \(n-(k+1)\) rather than \(n\)?
cards.back: Estimating \(k+1\) regression parameters creates dependencies among residuals, leaving only \(n-(k+1)\) unrestricted residuals.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex
